feedback.problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[-1,4]=[-1,0]\cup [0,3]\cup [3,4],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $5$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's plot what this function might look like, using the values given in the table.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14055663/assets/48212ed7c5cf3d8b6e523a98b91634320b8684c889e55d62ce4043f082f83cde.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-1)+f(0)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(3)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{3\text{rd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(3)+f(4)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{3}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{0+2}{2}\cdot (0-(-1))+\frac{2+4}{2}\cdot (3-0)+\frac{4+5}{2}\cdot (4-3) \\  & =1\cdot 1+3\cdot 3+\frac{9}{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =1+9+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{29}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
